YOUR DATA. YOUR DEVICE.

Privacy & permissions.

RepLock Android early access · Updated 23 October 2026.

What stays on your phone

RepLock stores your selected apps, preferences, coin balance, daily step totals, completed challenge count, active pass, and latest 100 wallet entries locally. No account, advertising SDK, or cloud wallet is included. Android app-data backup is disabled. Reset local progress in Setup or uninstall to remove this data.

Camera verification

Camera access is requested only when you start a challenge. Live images are processed on-device using bundled Google ML Kit pose detection to estimate body landmarks and count complete movements. RepLock does not record or upload photos or video. Camera processing pauses when the challenge leaves the foreground. ML Kit is a third-party library; consult Google’s ML Kit terms for its SDK data disclosures. RepLock itself has no analytics or advertising integration.

Pose estimates can miss reps. Good lighting, adequate space, and a full-body view help. They are not proof of identity, clinical assessment, or guaranteed fraud prevention. Use a comfortable range and stop if anything hurts. Steps provide an alternative way to earn coins.

Android Accessibility

After the in-app disclosure and your explicit permission, the Accessibility service observes foreground app identifiers and shows a blocking overlay for apps you select. Screen content retrieval is disabled. RepLock does not use it to read messages, posts, typed text, or passwords. App identifiers are not sent to a server. Pause App protection in Setup or disable the service in Android Settings at any time.

Protection is voluntary. Uninstalling, disabling Accessibility, device restrictions, or service interruption can prevent it. The app is not an unbreakable parental-control or security product. Leave essential apps unselected.

Step tracking

Optional activity-recognition permission allows the device step counter to track steps after activation. A foreground service displays a tracking notification. Notifications can be declined without granting camera access. No location or GPS is used. Steps before activation are not rewarded; gaps across midnight are conservatively discarded. Device reboots, battery restrictions, and service interruptions may require re-enabling tracking.

Coins & passes

Complete 10 squats for 20 coins, 15 jumping jacks for 30, or 20 alternating knee raises for 20. Camera rewards are limited to 200 coins/day with 45 seconds between completed sets. Each 500 tracked steps earns 5 coins, capped at 100 coins/day, claimed in the app. Local device time is used for daily limits, which are not a tamper-proof financial system.

A 5-, 10-, or 15-minute pass costs 10, 20, or 30 coins. One selected app is unlocked at a time. The timer starts at redemption and continues when you leave the app. Unused time is not refunded. Passes expire on reboot. Coins have no monetary value and cannot be bought, sold, or transferred.

This website & video

The walkthrough is a simulation and does not access your camera, apps, or steps. The website loads release metadata and the launch film from its hosting origin. The hosting provider may process normal access logs. A YouTube link opens YouTube, where Google’s own privacy policies apply. The app does not automatically upload content to YouTube.

Early access & iPhone

This Android test build is signed with a development key for sideload testing. A store release requires a private release key, store permission review, and physical-device validation. The iOS project is a UI preview; native iPhone enforcement and Apple entitlements are not released.
